title: Thematic analysis example: A worked walkthrough from transcript to theme
summary: Follow one thematic analysis example from 15 interviews to named themes, with excerpts that show the exact moment a code becomes a theme.
body_markdown:
What is an example of thematic analysis in qualitative research? +


A strong thematic analysis example traces one study, such as a representative 15-interview packaging study, from transcript to theme. Two themes cleared the study's working bar of roughly eight participants: premium design signaling higher prices among full-price buyers (10 of 15 participants) and loyal buyers disconnected from the modern aesthetic (nine of 15). The key patterns also showed sustainability expected rather than motivating, which stayed a supporting observation. The data analysis ran through familiarization, developing themes iteratively, and contradiction checks.


What format should a thematic analysis follow? +


A defensible thematic analysis format runs from raw data to defined codes to a named theme stated as a claim that answers the research questions. When reporting patterns, each theme carries verbatim quotes or source clips, because stakeholders cannot audit it otherwise. The format also lists negative cases: participants who contradict the pattern and limit the claim. Align code definitions first, or "price anxiety" and "packaging markup" cannot merge.


What does a thematic analysis table look like? +


A theme table is the most common data visualization in a qualitative analysis: it maps each transcript excerpt to its code, then to its theme. That mapping, along with visual tools like a code-to-theme diagram, makes the boundary call traceable. A prevalence table counts mentions, such as visual appeal in 80% of packaging interviews. The hybrid route turns validated themes into a fixed codebook, such as the two packaging themes applied to 50 more interviews across six markets, where cultural context shapes how participants voice the same reaction. The same codebook can then run across other data sources, such as open-ended survey responses.


How do you do thematic analysis on a single interview? +


On a single interview, code line by line and flag candidate themes, then test them against the rest of the study. A code becomes a theme only when its meaning recurs across all your transcripts, in other participants' words. The same rule applies to focus group transcripts: one vocal speaker is still one participant. Transcripts can misrepresent meaning by omitting pauses, tone, and facial expressions. Because analysts can watch the clip behind each quote, they catch the hesitation a transcript drops and the deeper insights behind it, and Conveo's multimodal analysis covers speech, tone and facial cues across every session. Researchers still inspect and correct the AI coding, check the clips behind each theme, and run negative case checks as part of the method.


Does a thesis thematic analysis example apply to enterprise research? +


A thematic analysis example from a thesis teaches the right discipline. Academic work often follows reflexive thematic analysis and anchors themes to existing literature, while enterprise teams anchor them to research objectives and a business decision, under tighter constraints. Either way, deciding when codes become a theme is the hardest step in any qualitative research project, often made by instinct. Analyzing qualitative data by hand strains as interview counts grow. With Conveo's integrated panel network supporting data collection and AI-assisted first-pass coding, analysts shift their time from line-by-line tagging to validation.
